de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking') · also de — 'with' of manner (de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'); 'on' (de pie 'on foot'); 'from' of side (della e della part 'from both sides'); de cabo 'anew' (de + cabo, 'again'); de suso de 'above'; seños … de seños colpes 'with one blow each' · also de — 'in respect of' after an adjective (sobejana de mala 'exceedingly bad'); 'with regard to, about' (me plaze de mio Çid 'I am pleased about the Cid'); 'from, at the hand of' (de señor non ha graçia 'he gets no favor from a lord'); 'from' of origin (de moros fo 'it came from Moors'); 'at' of manner (de vagar 'at leisure', de + the noun vagar) · also de’ — Pidal's de’llaño, read as del llaño 'of the plain' (the article's l run into the ll; a reading, not certain) · de + infinitive after an adjective (de ir somos guisados 'we are ready to go') · also de + infinitive after a verb: començar de 'to begin to' (compeçó de fablar 'he began to speak'), piénssanse de 'set about' (piénssanse de armar), aver de 'to have to' (lo que ha de far 'what he has to do') · also de — 'within' of a time limit (De aquestos quinze días, most likely 'within these fifteen days'; sense uncertain); de veluntad 'willingly'; de + superlative partitive (de los mejores guarnimientos 'of the best equipment') · also de — 'with, from' of the means or source (diziendo de la boca 'saying with his mouth'; de cuer les pesa 'it grieves them from the heart') · also de que 'of whom, of which' (relative after a noun; de moros de que non avien sabor 'of Moors they had no taste for') · de firme 'steadfastly, with a will' (de firme robavan el campo); de + noun of material, 'in' (de plata seys çientos marcos 'six hundred marks in silver'); of possession, 'belonging to' (de vos son 'are yours'); fartos de lidiar 'sated with fighting'; pagado de 'pleased with' · also de — dé, may he give (present subjunctive 3rd sg. of dar, printed without accent; que vos de dent buen galardón 'that he may give you a good reward for it'; = dé) · also tanto … de + adjective, 'so (very)' (tanto son de traspuestas 'so far gone are they')
los: el — the (masc. pl.); them (object pronoun) · also los que 'those who' (demonstrative use before a relative); los — him, them as object of consejar (commo los consejava 'as he advised them') · also los de 'those of' (con los de Castejón 'with the men of Castejón')
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold') · also aver — 'I will', the future auxiliary in a split future (quitarvos e … darvos e de mano 'I will free you … I will let you go'; = vos quitaré, vos daré) · also the full verb 'I have' (el sabor que dend e 'the delight I have of it') · also e — pleonastic 'and' joining two names of the one person (a Dios e al padre 'to God, the Father'; Pidal 'conjunción e pleonástica', cf. v. 300)
álbar: Álbar — Álvar (personal name, Álbar Fáñez; = Álvar)
per: Per — Pero, short for Pedro (Per Vermudoz = Pedro Bermúdez, a vassal of the Cid)
otro: otro — other, another (masc.; el otro 'the other'; = otro) · also otro día 'the next day'; lo otro 'the rest'
tanto: tanto — so much, so great · tanto quanto + subjunctive 'as long as' (tanto quanto yo biva 'as long as I live') · also tanto — 'so many' before a masc. sg. noun used collectively (tanto palafré, tanto buen pendón 'so many a palfrey, so many a good banner'; = tantos) · also dos tanto — 'twice as much' (que vos meresca dos tanto 'that I may deserve it of you twice over'; = el doble)
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha) · ha — to (a with h-, aver a + inf. 'will, must': lo an todos ha far 'all are to do it'); aver — has, possesses (las fijas que ha 'the daughters she has') · also ha — future ending after infinitive + clitics, the split future (tornar nos la ha 'he will give it back to us'; = nos la tornará) · also ha — there is, there are (impersonal; dos señas ha cabdales 'there are two chief banners'; = hay) · also ha — perfect auxiliary 'has' before the participle (ha vendido 'has sold'; fechos los ha ricos 'has made them rich') · also 'has, gets' (de señor non ha graçia 'he has no favor from a lord') · also ha de + inf. 'is to' (que los ha de aguardar 'who is to attend them'; aver de + infinitive, = ha de) · also non ha qui + inf. — 'there is no one to' (impersonal ha 'there is'; non ha qui tomallos 'there is no one to take them'; = no hay quien) · also ha — of time elapsed, 'it is, it has been' (Pocos días ha … que 'it is a few days since'; = hace)
don: don — don, lord (honorific title) · also don — gift (noun; en don 'as a gift') · also don — from where, whence (= donde, de onde; Castejón don abremos grand enpara 'Castejón, from which we shall have great protection') · 'whereof, with which' (Pidal 'de lo cual'; don yo sea pagado 'whereof I may be satisfied') · also don — when, where (= donde, of time; Don llegan los otros 'when the others come up')
elvira: Elvira — Elvira, one of the Cid's two daughters (doña Elvira, also printed don Elvira; = Elvira)
doña: doña — lady (title; Latin domina, fem. of don)
sol: sol — sun · also 'even, so much as' (sol non 'not even'; sol non será penssado 'it will not even be thought of') · also sol — so + l, 'under the' (so 'under', Latin sub, + el before a vowel): del sol espada 'from under the sword' (the likeliest reading; the construction is uncertain) · also Sol — doña Sol, one of the Cid's two daughters (personal name) · also sol — so + el, 'under the' (metiós sol esçaño 'he got under the bench'; here the sense is clear)
ayades: aver — you may have (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -des ending; = hayáis)
vos: vos — you (object pronoun, polite/plural) · also subject 'you' (vos, que por mí dexades 'you who leave for my sake'); dative 'to you' (dar vos quiero vuestra part) · also reflexive/ethic 'you (yourselves)' (id vos en algara 'go off on a raid'); dative with an impersonal sense (si cueta vos fore 'if need befall you') · also vos — stressed 'you' after a preposition (parto de vos 'I part from you'; abiltaredes a vos 'you will dishonor yourselves')
sodes: seer — you are (2nd pl. present, used respectfully to one person; = sois; old -edes ending, cf. odredes, vedes, catedes)
sanas: sano — sound, unharmed, healthy (fem. pl.; sanas e sin mal 'safe and unharmed'; = sanas)
bivas: bivo — alive (fem. pl.; non por bivas 'not as living'; = vivas)
sin: sin — without · also sin — 'besides, apart from' (sin las peonadas 'besides the foot-soldiers'); sin falla 'without fail'; sin dubda
mal: mal — harm, hurt, ruin · mal — evil, in the prayer's sense (por end es salvo de mal 'therefore he is saved from evil') · also mal — adverb 'sorely, ill' (por cuer le pesó mal 'it grieved him sorely at heart') · also tener a mal — 'to take amiss' (non lo tenga a mal 'let him not take it amiss') · also mal — evil, bad (adjective, apocopated malo, before a noun; mal galardón 'an evil reward'; = mal)
casamiento: casamiento — marriage, match, wedding alliance (= casamiento)
mejor: mejor — better, best (adverb; quanto ella mejor sabe 'as best she knows how'; = mejor) · also mejor — better (adjective; oy es día bueno e mejor será cras 'today is a good day and tomorrow will be better') · also mejor — best (comparative as superlative, after the noun; coranado mejor 'the best churchman'; = el mejor)
podredes: poder — you will be able (future 2nd pl., syncopated for poderedes; hi los podredes fallar 'you will be able to find them there'; = podréis)
ganar: ganar — to gain, earn · also 'to capture, take (a fortress)' (Alcoçer cueda ganar 'he expects to take Alcocer') · also ganar — to till, work the land (Pidal, like Old French gaignier; non se treven ganar 'they dare not work their fields'; = labrar)
aun: aun — even, besides · also aun — yet, still (aun vea el dia 'may I yet see the day') · also 'even though' (= aunque; aun de lo que diessen oviessen grand ganançia, Pidal's reading)
veamos: veer — (that) we may see (present subjunctive 1st pl., optative; muchos dias vos veamos 'may we see you for many days'; = veamos)
el: el — the (masc.) · also el — 'he who' before a relative (el qui quisiere, el que es sobre Fenares); el before a fem. noun beginning with a vowel (el espada = la espada; el algara = la algara) · also el de + place name 'he of, the one from' (mio Çid el de Bivar)
que: que — that, who, which; for · also por que — because, since (= porque) · por que — by which, whereby (por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more') · also que — 'so that, lest' introducing purpose/result (que por miedo non dexen nada; por tal lo faze … que no lo ventasse nadi); after después/mientra 'after, while' (después que, mientra que) · also que — than, after a comparative (mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him') · also que — what (indirect interrogative; dezir vos he que faze 'I shall tell you what he does'; = qué) · also que — how, exclamative before an adverb (Dios, que bien los sirvió! 'God, how well he served them!'; = qué)
í: í — there (adverb, Latin ibi; í albergaron 'there they lodged'; = allí; survives in the 'y' of hay)
yazen: yazer — they lie (present 3rd pl.; yazen muertos 'they lie dead'; = yacen)
fazen: fazer — they make, give (present 3rd pl.; grand yantar le fazen 'they give him a great feast'; = hacen) · also fazerse — to become (cavalleros se fazen 'they become knights'; = se hacen) · also fazerse — passive 'are made' (las moradas cómmo se fazen 'how the dwellings are made'; sense of moradas uncertain)
mañana: mañana — morning (a la mañana 'in the morning'; otro dia mañana 'next morning'; = mañana) · also mañana — early, soon (adverb/predicate; mucho es mañana 'it is too soon (to take back a man in disgrace after only three weeks)'; = pronto, temprano)
pienssan: pensar — they think; pensar de + inf. 'to set about (doing)' (epic formula)
estevan: Estevan — Esteban, i.e. San Esteban de Gormaz, a town on the Duero
van: ir — they go (present 3rd pl.) · also ir + gerund 'keep going' (passando van 'they go on passing') · also ir + infinitive 'go to' (le van çercar 'they go to besiege him'; se van tornar 'they go back')
fata: fata — until, as far as (variant of fasta; = hasta)
d: de — of, with (elided form of de before a vowel, d'arena = de arena) · de — from (unos d'otros 'one from another') · also d — 'about, concerning' (D' iffantes de Carrión yo vos quiero contar 'of the Infantes of Carrión I wish to tell you'; = de)
amor: amor — love; por amor de 'for the love of' · also amor — favour, grace of a lord toward his vassal (davos su amor 'he gives you his favour'; del rey he su amor 'I have the king's favour') · also amor — good will, consent (of a vassal to his lord's act; con vuestro amor 'with your good will') · also amor — favour, kindness done at a request (Si este amor non feches 'if you do not grant this favour'; = favor)
allent: allent — beyond, on the far side of (apocopated allende; de alle[n]t partes del mar 'from beyond the sea'; = allende; also in d'allent mar)
se: se — himself/herself/itself (reflexive pronoun) · also se — passive 'is, are' (cómmo se gana el pan 'how bread is earned'; = se, passive-reflexive) · also se — ethic/intensive dative 'for himself, with his own eyes' (él se lo vío con los ojos 'he saw it himself')
dellos: de + ellos — of them, from them (contraction)
piénssanse: pensar + se — they set about (present 3rd pl. + reflexive; piénssanse de adobar 'they set about getting ready'; = se ponen a)
tornar: tornar — to return; tornar palabra 'to answer a word' · also tornar — 'to give back' (tornar nos la ha doblada 'will give it back to us doubled'; infinitive + enclitic + ha, future); to turn (round), transitive (mandó tornar la seña 'he had the banner turned about')
minaya: Minaya — the title by which the Cid's kinsman Álvar Fáñez is called, usually explained as mi + anaya 'my brother'
con: con — with · also con — 'with the help of' (con Dios 'with God's help'; verlo hemos con Dios 'we shall see it with God's help') · also con — 'up to, as high as' (las ramas pujan con las nuoves 'the branches climb up to the clouds', Pidal 'suben hasta las nubes')
iva: ir — he was going (imperfect 3rd sg.; iva posar 'was going to halt'; = iba) · ir + gerund, progressive 'was gradually doing' (yas iva alegrando 'was already cheering up'; miedo iva aviendo 'was going along with fear')
cabadelant: cabadelant — straight on, forward, onward (adverb, cab (= cabo 'head, end') + adelant, apocopated; aguijó cabadelant 'he spurred on ahead'; = adelante, derecho adelante)
troçieron: troçir — they passed, went by (preterite 3rd pl.; Troçieron a Santa María 'they passed Santa María'; cf. tres an por troçir; no modern form)
gormaz: Gormaz — Gormaz, castle on the Duero (Pidal: its great castle is from the Arab period and was of capital importance in the tenth-century reconquest; un castiello tan fuort 'a castle so strong'; = Gormaz)
o: o — or; also ó — where (interrogative, Latin ubi; ¿O sodes…? 'Where are you…?') · also o — where (relative adverb; o dizen Castejón 'which they call Castejón'; o el Campeador estava 'where the Campeador was'; = donde) · correlative 'either … or' (o me dexaredes … o … levaredes 'either you will leave me … or you will take away')
dizen: dezir — they say, they call (present 3rd pl.; do dizen monte Calvarie 'where they call (it) Mount Calvary'; = dicen)
ivan: ir — they were going (imperfect 3rd pl.; ivan posar 'they were going to lodge'; = iban) · also ir + gerund, 'were coming to, gradually' (ya lo ivan provando 'they were by now coming to experience it')
passar: passar — to cross, pass over (infinitive; = pasar) · also passar — 'to pass through, pierce' (tanta adágara foradar e passar 'so many shields pierced and passed through') · also noun el passar 'the crossing' (en el passar de Xúcar 'at the crossing of the Júcar'; = el paso)
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado) · personal a before a direct object (salvest a Jonás; a ti adoro); a + inf. 'to, about to' (tornólas a catar); a tan grand sabor 'with so great pleasure'; a ojo 'in plain sight' · also a — 'into' (sacar a çelada 'to lure into ambush'); 'at, in' (a la çaga 'at the rear'); 'against' (dar salto a la çaga); dative 'to' (a mí dedes); haber a + inf. 'have to' (lo han a far); a + noun of direction (adeliñava a la puerta 'made for the gate') · impersonal 'there is' (aver; es dia a de plazo 'there is (only) a day of the term', the most likely reading of a hard line); ha as auxiliary set after the participle (soñado a 'he has dreamt') · also 'on, at (a time)' (a tercer dia 'on the third day') · also a — 'has' before the participle, agreeing with the object (la lança a quebrada 'he has broken the lance'; a menester 'has need of'); a + dative of the person affected (a Minaya matáronle el cavallo 'they killed Minaya's horse') · a — 'as, for' (tóvoslo a grand fonta 'he took it as a great affront') · also a — 'with' of instrument (a dientes las tomó 'with his teeth he took them'; = con) · also prender a espolonada — 'to begin the attack, charge' (priso a espolonada, Pidal 'comenzó el ataque'); pendón a corças 'a banner with (a device of) roe-does' (a = 'with', likely)
la: el/la — the (fem.); her/it (object pronoun) · also la que 'the one that' (Çelfa la que dizen de Canal 'Çelfa, the one they call of the Canal')
casa: casa — house; also settlement, town (Burgos la casa 'the town of Burgos') · also casar — he marries (off) (present 3rd sg.; él vos casa 'it is he who marries you off'; = casa)
presa: prender — taken (past part. fem.; la paria que a presa 'the tribute he has taken'; = prendida, tomada)
han: aver — they have (present 3rd pl.; = han); after an infinitive, the auxiliary of a split future (seervos han = os serán) · also han a + inf. 'they have to, are bound to' (mandado de so señor todo lo han a far); 'they hold, possess' (que moros las han) · also perfect auxiliary 'have' with a participle agreeing with its object (la ganançia que han fecha 'the booty they have made')
andar: andar — to travel, go on (infinitive; = andar) · also andar a alguien — to act for someone, stand by him (andar le quiero a mio Çid en toda pro, Pidal 'quiero ayudar al Cid en cuanto pueda')
qual: qual — which (relative/interrogative adjective; de qual part 'from whichever side'; = cual)
medina: Medina — Medinaceli, the frontier town on the Jalón where Alfonso's land ends (= Medinaceli)
albergar: albergar — to lodge, halt for the night (infinitive; iva albergar 'went to lodge', i.e. lodged; = albergar, closest alojarse, acampar)
molina: Molina — Molina (de Aragón), town in the province of Guadalajara (= Molina)
en: en — in, into, on · en — of it, thence (= ende; por en avemos qué fablar 'of which we have to speak') · also en — 'as' (en paria 'as tribute'); en essora 'at that moment' · also en — 'among' (en todos los sos 'among all his men') · also en + infinitive 'in (doing)' (en levarlo adelant 'in carrying it forward'); en çinco días 'in five days'
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least' · also a + el standing for a + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (al espada = a la espada) · also al — 'other thing, the rest' (neuter, Latin alius; de lo al non pienssan nada 'of anything else they think nothing'; distinct from a + el) · also a + el before an infinitive 'on, upon' (al exir de Salón 'on leaving the Jalón'; = al salir) · al 'the other thing, the rest' in al feredes adelant 'the rest you will do later' · also por al 'otherwise, for any other reason' (non passará por al 'it will not be otherwise'); a mí mandedes al 'order me something else', give me another charge (the likelier reading of a terse line)
moro: moro — Moor, Muslim (noun; el moro Avengalvón 'the Moor Avengalvón'; = moro)
avengalvón: Avengalvón — the Moorish lord (alcaide) of Molina, friend and ally of the Cid (proper name, Aven- = Arabic ibn 'son of'; = Abengalbón)
coraçón: coraçón — heart (= corazón) · also por coraçón 'willingly, heartily, with a will' (lo an por coraçón) · also de coraçón 'heartily, with a will' (adóbanse de coraçón 'they arm with a will')
le: le — to him, him (dative pronoun) · also le — him, as direct object (leísmo; si ellos le prenden 'if they take him'); dative (non se le dava 'did not surrender to him') · also le — dative of separation, 'from him' (que nos le parte de so braço 'who does not leave his side'); dative 'for him' (ques le non spidiés 'who does not take leave of him')
plaz: plazer — it pleases (present 3rd sg., apocopated; a todos plaz 'it pleases all'; = place, closest agrada)
saliólos: salir + los — he went out to (them) (preterite salió + enclitic los; saliólos reçebir 'went out to welcome them'; = salió a recibirlos)
buena: bueno — good (fem.); en buen(a) '(born/girded) in a good hour' — the poem's honorific formula
voluntad: voluntad — will, willingness; de voluntad e de grado, a doubled formula, 'willingly and gladly' · God's will (commo fo tu voluntad 'as was your will'); de toda voluntad 'with all one's heart' · also de buena voluntad 'gladly, willingly' (the formula of assent); a toda su voluntad 'wholly to his satisfaction, at his will' · also damor e de voluntad 'with love and good will, gladly' (the formula of assent)
por: por — through, along, by, for · purpose, 'in order to' (por el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'); por + inf. 'yet to be done' (tres an por troçir 'three remain to pass'); 'for, on behalf of' (por mio Çid) · also por — 'out of, because of' (por miedo 'through fear'); 'for (that reason)' (por tal lo faze 'he does it for that reason'); 'by way of' (por Guadalfajara); por + noun 'for the sake of' ; por coraçón 'willingly' · also 'for (a price)' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'by means of' (por carta 'by writ'); 'through, thanks to' (por mí ganaredes 'through me you will gain') · also por — 'on, during (a time)' (por aquesta mañana 'this morning'); 'by way of, through' (por medio de la llaña 'through the middle of the plain') · also por — 'in' after fiar (yo fío por Dios 'I trust in God') · also por — 'to fetch, for' after enbiar/ir (enbiaré por ellas, irán por ellas 'I shall send for them', 'they will go for them'); por cuenta 'by count, in a count' · also por — as (por heredad 'as a possession') · also por — 'about, after' with preguntar (por el rey tómanse a preguntar 'they begin to ask after the king'); por + infinitive 'for … to' (por … vençer reyes, 'for … to defeat kings') · also por — 'in requital for, to avenge' (nos vengaremos aquesta por la del león 'we shall avenge this one for the lion affair'); por muertas 'for dead, as dead'; por lo que 'for what, on account of what'
mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
les: les — to them · also les — 'from them', dative of removal or injury (les tollió el pan 'took the bread from them'; viédales exir 'forbids them to go out')
da: dar — he gives (present 3rd sg.; nin da conssejo padre a fijo 'neither does father give help to son'; = da)
dent: dent — of it, thereof (de + ent, a form of ende 'thence'; non nos darán dent nada 'they will give us none of it'; = de ello) · also dent — from there, thence (dent corre mio Çid a Huesa 'from there the Çid raids to Huesa'; = de allí)
valençia: Valençia — Valencia, the Moorish kingdom and city whose king Tamín is addressed (= Valencia) · also Valençia — the city itself, held by the Cid (en Valençia sedí mio Çid 'in Valencia was my Cid'; Valençia vienen çercar 'they come to besiege Valencia')
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour' · al ora 'at that very hour, then' (en ti crovo al ora) · also una grant ora — a long while (Pidal 'un gran rato'; = un buen rato)
nasco: nacer — he was born (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = nació)
llegava: llegar — it was arriving, was reaching (imperfect 3rd sg.; el mensaje llegava 'the message was reaching (him)'; = llegaba)
menssaje: menssaje — message, the news or word sent (noun, ss = s; = mensaje)
reçebirlos: reçebir + los — to receive them (infinitive + enclitic los; = recibirlos)
sale: salir — he goes out (present 3rd sg.; = sale)
armas: arma — weapon, arms (pl.; armas de lidiar 'weapons for fighting'; en armas 'in arms, armed'; = armas) · also armas — men-at-arms, armed men (treynta mill de armas 'thirty thousand armed men') · also armas — armour, defensive gear (nol falssan las armas 'they do not pierce his armour'); armas de señal 'arms with a device' (see señal)
teniendo: tener — holding (gerund; teniendo a la çaga 'holding the rearguard'; = teniendo) · also tener armas 'to play at arms', mock combat in display (teniendo salien armas, Pidal 'salían jugando las armas'; comp. v. 1577)
faze: fazer — is done, is made (present 3rd sg.; = hace) · also fazer — he does, makes (active present 3rd sg.; por tal lo faze mio Çid 'for that reason Mio Cid does it'; = hace)
amas: amos — both (fem. pl., Latin ambas; las manos amas 'both hands'; = ambas)
tornós: tornar + se — she turned back (tornó + -s(e): after a stressed vowel -se shrinks to -s) · also tornarse a + inf. 'to set to, begin' (tornós a sonrisar 'he broke into a smile', perhaps 'smiled again'; the Cid the subject) · also he turned (toward) (tornós a essa part 'he turned that way', the Cid the subject) · also tornós — he turned back (the -s from se; Por el rastro tornós Félez Muñoz 'back along the trail Félez Muñoz turned'; masc. subject, not 'she')
sonrrisar: sonrrisar — to smile (infinitive; tornós a sonrrisar 'he began to smile'; = sonreír)
venides: venir — you come (2nd pl. present, old -des ending; = venís)
dios: Dios — God · also Dios! — interjection of wonder (Dios, cómmo se alabavan! 'God, how they boasted!')
curie: curiar — may (God) guard (present subjunctive 3rd sg.; no modern curiar, = guarde)
mas: mas — but · also mas — 'most' (superlative, = más; en todo lo mas alto 'on the very highest part') · also mas — 'more' comparative (que es mas ondrada 'which is more honored'; = más)
plega: plazer — may it please (present subjunctive 3rd sg.; plega a Dios 'may it please God'; = plazca)
vea: veer — may I/he see (present subjunctive 1st/3rd sg.; = vea)
casadas: casar — married, settled in marriage (past part. fem. pl.; tener por casadas 'to count themselves married'; = casadas)
aquí: aquí — here; d'aquí 'from here' · also 'then, at this point' (aquí dixo el comde 'then the count said')
adelant: adelant — onward, ahead (apocopated adverb; = adelante) · also adelant — henceforth, from now on (of time; mio reyno adelant 'the rest of my reign'); ir adelant 'to prosper, go forward' (las nuevas del Çid mucho van adelant; = prosperar)
carrión: Carrión — Carrión de los Condes, town in Palencia, seat of the counts of Carrión (= Carrión)
me: me — me, to me · also reflexive 'myself' (fata que yo me pague 'until I am satisfied')
faga: fazer — may I/he make, cause (present subjunctive 1st/3rd sg.; = haga); faga cantar 'have sung'
manos: mano — hand (pl.); dar las manos = the handclasp that makes an agreement binding · a las manos 'for the hands' (pidió agua a las manos 'asked for water to wash his hands'); bolver las manos 'to ply the hands', busy eating · also a las manos tomar 'to take by the hand' (a las manos les tomó, Pidal 'los tomó de la mano')
padre: padre — father · el Padre santo, God the Father
fizo: fazer — he made, did, caused (strong preterite 3rd sg.; fizo posar 'he made (them) halt'; = hizo)
ellas: ella — they, them (fem. pl., stressed; con ellas 'with them'; = ellas)
su: su — his, her, its · also su — their (aquella su almofalla 'that host of theirs')
quiso: querer — he wished (strong preterite 3rd sg.; non quiso 'he did not want'; = quiso)
sos: so — his, her, their (= modern sus) · also los sos 'his own men' (possessive with article as noun; en todos los sos 'among all his men')
poridad: poridad — secrecy, privacy, confidence (= puridad); en poridad 'in confidence' · also poridad — secret council, secret plan (aviendo su poridad 'holding their secret talk'; con esta poridad 'with this secret plan')
penssó: pensar — he set about (preterite 3rd sg.; pensar de + inf. 'to set about doing'; = pensó) · also pensar — he thought, considered (preterite 3rd sg.; penssó e comidió 'he thought and pondered'; = pensó)
enbiar: enbiar — to send (infinitive; fizo enbiar por la tienda 'he had (someone) send for the tent'; = enviar)
muño: Muño — personal name (Muño Gustioz, a vassal of the Cid; = Munio, an old name; Nuño is probably related)
gustioz: Gustioz — patronymic 'son of Gustio' (Muño Gustioz, the Cid's retainer, brought up in his household; = Gustioz, no modern form)
pro: pro — worth, merit; de pro 'worthy, of good standing' · also pro — profit, advantage, benefit (grant pro les fazié 'he did them great good, was of great profit to them') · also pro — useful, of worth (adjective; en lo al non es tan pro 'in other things he is not so worthy')
te: te — you, thee (2nd sg. object pronoun) · also te — reflexive 'yourself' (non te juntarás 'you will not join yourself, come up with'; = te)
tí: tú — thee (stressed object pronoun; = ti, old accentuation)
mi: mi — my (unstressed possessive) · also mi — me (stressed pronoun after a preposition; por mi 'on my behalf'; = mí)
cort: cort — court, royal or lordly household (fem. noun; en mi cort 'in my court'; = corte)
mandado: mandado — message, news, word (noun; from mandar 'to send, order') · also mandado — order, command (mandado de so señor 'the lord's command'); fazer mandado 'to send word' · also past part. 'granted, assigned' (el quinto que me avedes mandado 'the fifth you have granted me') · also past part. 'ordered, charged' after aver (que a mí lo ovo mandado 'who had charged me with it'); with gelo he mandado 'I have promised it to him' (Pidal 'otorgado, o prometido') under 'granted'
mano: mano — hand (sg.); en vuestra mano = 'in your keeping' · a mano 'by hand, hand-picked' (escollechos a mano 'chosen by hand') · dar de mano 'to let go, release' (Pidal 'soltar'; darvos e de mano 'I will let you go')
quomo: commo — as (variant spelling, Pidal's Qu[o]mo; = como)
so: so/su — his, her, its (unstressed possessive sg.; so çervicio = su servicio); also seer — I am (1st sg. present; = soy; so ayrado, 'I am in [the king's] ira') · lo so — 'what is his, his own' (neuter article + possessive; lo so puede menguar 'what is his may dwindle') · also so — their (so consejo 'their counsel', so vino 'their wine'; = su)
elle: elle — he (old form of él, Latin ille; elle fizo = él hizo; Pidal restores el[le]) · also el[le] after a preposition, 'it, him' (en el[le] 'in it', of the hat; en el[le] fincan los ojos 'they fix their eyes on him'; = él)
es: seer — it is (present 3rd sg.) · also ser as perfect auxiliary of intransitives (exido es 'has gone out') and passive auxiliary (la tienda es cogida) · also es — that (apocopated esse = ese, demonstrative; en es alcaz 'in that pursuit', por es logar 'through that place')
desta: de + esta — of this (preposition de + demonstrative fem. sg.; desta batalla 'of this battle'; = de esta)
desondra: desondra — dishonor, outrage (fem., des- + onra; la desondra del león 'the dishonor of the lion'; = deshonra)
an: aver — they have (3rd pl. present of aver = han) · perfect auxiliary (passados los an 'they have passed'; la missa acabada la an 'they have finished'); an por troçir 'there remain to pass'; an ... ha far 'they have to do, are to do' · also future auxiliary after an infinitive, the split future (ve[e]rme an 'they will see me'; = me verán)
fecha: fazer — made, done (past part. fem. of fazer = hacer; = hecha, note f-)
ifantes: infante — young nobleman, son of a noble house (pl., spelt Ifantes; = infantes)
quel: que + le — who ... him (que + enclitic/elided le) · that ... to him (quel creçe conpaña 'that company grows for him')
ca: ca — for, because (Latin quia) · ca — perhaps 'but, whereas' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró allá; the sense is uncertain) · also ca non — 'and not that' (Pidal 'y no que'; cuédanse que es almofalla, ca non vienen con mandado 'they think it is an army, and not that they come with a message')
gelas: ge + las — them for/to him (ge, ancestor of modern se, + las; = se las) · also ge 'to them' (non gelas do yo 'I do not give them to them')
dexadas: dexar — left (past part. fem. pl.; las puertas an dexadas 'they have left the gates'; = dejadas)
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!' · si non — otherwise, if not (si non, do sopiéredes 'if not, wherever you learn'); si + future subjunctive 'if' (si nos falláredes 'if you find us') · also si — si'nulla = sin + nulla with -n assimilated before n- (si'nulla dubda 'without any fear' (or 'doubt'); = sin ningún miedo, sin ninguna duda) · also si non — 'except, but for' (si non a estos cavalleros 'except these knights'; = salvo) · also si — 'so', optative, = sí, with the present subjunctive in an adjuration (si vos vala el Criador 'so may the Creator help you')
y: y — and (rarer spelling of e) · also y — there (adverb, = i, Latin ibi; entraré y 'I shall enter there')
contra: contra — toward, facing, in the direction of (= hacia; contra la sierra 'facing the sierra')
nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us') · also reflexive 'ourselves' (nos partimos 'we part'); dative (la missa nos dirá 'will say for us') · also nos' — non + se (aun nos' van del campo 'they are still not leaving the field'; the apostrophe marks the elision) · also nos — non + se, written without apostrophe (nin amigo a amigo nos pueden consolar 'nor can friend console friend'; mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him', the no redundant after the comparison) · also nos — stressed 'us' after a preposition (daxadas seredes de nos 'you will be abandoned by us'; sobre nos 'upon us'); stressed repeated subject (mártires seremos nos 'we shall be martyrs')
averes: aver — goods, possessions, wealth (aver as noun, pl.)
sobejanos: sobejano — excessive, abundant beyond measure (masc. pl. adj.)
son: seer — they are (3rd pl.) · also son — perfect auxiliary of intransitives and passive auxiliary (todos son exidos 'have all gone out'; nombrados son; son derramadas 'are scattered')
esso: esso — that (neuter demonstrative; esso con esto 'that together with this'; = eso)
pesar: pesar — grief, sorrow (noun; = pesar) · also pesar — to grieve (infinitive; non me a por qué pesar 'there is nothing to grieve me in it'; = pesar)
otra: otro — other (fem. sg.; del otra part 'on the other side', with el before a vowel-initial feminine noun, = de la otra parte)
vistas: vistas — meeting, interview of persons (fem. pl. noun; a vistas 'to a meeting'; = vistas, entrevista)
cortes: corte — court, royal assembly (fem. pl.; en vistas o en cortes 'at meetings or at courts'; = cortes)
commo: commo — as, like (spelling variant of como) · how, that, in the way that (commo sirva a doña Ximena 'how he is to serve doña Ximena'); like (commo la uña de la carne) · also commo si + imperfect subjunctive — 'as if' (commo si escapasse 'as if he were fleeing') · commo que 'as one who' (commo que ira a de rey … es echado 'as one who has the king's anger and is cast out') · also commo — 'as soon as, when' (commo gelo a dicho 'as soon as he told it him'); 'since, as' (commo fío por Dios 'as I trust in God')
aya: aver — I may have (present subjunctive 1st sg.; = haya) · also aya — he may have (present subjunctive 3rd sg., same form as 1st; de Dios aya su graçia 'may he have God's grace', optative; = haya)
derecho: derecho — right, justice; satisfaction owed (noun; derecho me avrá a dar 'he will have to give me redress'; = derecho)
rencura: rencura — grievance, sorrow, complaint (fem.; toda nuestra rencura 'all our grievance'; = rencor, queja)
cavalgó: cavalgar — he rode (preterite 3rd sg.; = cabalgó) · also cavalgar — he set (them) on horseback (transitive; las cavalgó 'he mounted them'; = las montó)
él: él — he (stressed subject pronoun) · also él — 'him, it' after a preposition, of a thing (a él vino; en él fincaredes 'in it', i.e. in Castejón)
dos: dos — two · also do + se, 'when/where … (they)' (Dos fallan con los moros 'when they come upon the Moors', Pidal 'cuando se encuentran'; = cuando se encuentran) · also do + se, 'where … (he might)' with a subjunctive (non vido … dos alçasse 'he saw nowhere he might hide', Pidal 'donde se escondiese')
sirvan: servir — they may serve (present subjunctive 3rd pl.; que sirvan a so señor 'that they serve their lord'; = sirvan)
sabor: sabor — pleasure, wish; a so sabor 'at his (their) pleasure' · also por sabor de 'out of a wish to please, for the sake of' (por sabor de mio Çid 'to please the Cid') · also por sabor que — 'out of the desire (that)' (por sabor que avía de algún moro matare 'out of the longing I had to kill some Moor') · also aver sabor — to long for, to wish (lo que avía sabor 'what I longed for'; a qui yo ovier sabor 'to whomever I please', Pidal 'quisiere') · also mal sabor — pain, distress (don ellas an mal sabor 'from which they have pain'); sin sabor — 'without pleasure, without mercy' (májanlas tan sin sabor 'they beat them so without mercy'; sense perhaps)
criazón: criazón — household, those reared in a lord's house (fem. collective; los de criazón 'the household folk', Pidal 'sus familiares, las personas criadas en su casa'; = criados)
salien: salir — they were leaving, came out (imperfect 3rd pl. in -ién; Salien de Valençia 'they were leaving Valencia'; = salían)
andan: andar — they go about, range (present 3rd pl.; = andan)
quanto: quanto — as much as, whatever (= cuanto) · quanto ella mejor sabe 'as best she can' (quanto + comparative 'as much as') · also 'how much' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'as far/fast as' (quanto pueden andar) · tanto quanto 'as long as'; por quanto … ha 'for all that there is' (por quanto en el mundo ha) · also en quanto — 'as far as, insofar as' (En quanto podemos 'as far as we are able'; = en cuanto)
puoden: poder — they can (present 3rd pl., Pidal's pu[o]den with the diphthong; nada dezir non puoden 'they cannot say anything'; = pueden)
dan: dar — they give (present 3rd pl.; vagar non se dan 'they allow themselves no leisure'; = dan) · also dar — 'to pay (tribute)' (dan parias 'they pay tribute')
vagar: vagar — leisure, slowness (noun; de vagar 'at leisure, unhurriedly'; = vagar, closest despacio)
noches: noche — night (fem. pl.; las noches e los días 'nights and days'; = noches)
fagunt: Fagunt — Sahagún, the monastery town in León (San Fagunt = San Facundo; Fagunt apocopated; = Sahagún)
lo: lo — him, it (object pronoun) · lo que perdedes 'that which you lose' (neuter antecedent of the relative) · also lo — neuter article 'what is' (lo to 'what is yours'); pleonastic 'it' (lo an, lo han a far; por tal lo faze 'for that reason he does it')
falló: fallar — he found (preterite 3rd sg.; quando los falló 'when he had found them (all assembled)'; = halló)
león: León — León, the kingdom and city (Alfons el de León 'Alfonso of León'; = León) · also león — lion, the animal (masc.; saliós … el león 'the lion broke loose', adeliñó para' león 'he made straight for the lion'; = león), not the kingdom
bien: bien — well · bien — good, benefit (noun; algún bien vos pueda far 'some good I may do you') · bien — very, quite, intensifying an adverb (bien çerca del agua 'very near the water')
san: santo — Saint (apocopated before a name; = san)
fasta: fasta — until, as far as (= hasta)
santi: santi — saint (old form before a saint's name, from Latin sancti as in Sancti Iacobi, which survives fused in Santiago; santi Yagüe 'Saint James'; = santo, san)
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision') · also todo — adverbial 'wholly, all over' before an adjective (todo suzio 'all filthy')
ellos: ellos — they, them (stressed 3rd pl. masc. pronoun)
comdes: conde — counts (pl., Pidal's co[m]des; de comdes de Carrión 'of the counts of Carrión'; = condes)
tienen: tener — they have, hold, carry (present 3rd pl.; todas tienen pendones 'all carry pennons'; = tienen) · also tenerse por — to count oneself (ques tienen por casadas 'who count themselves married'; = se tienen por) · also tener por — to hold (someone) to be (muchos tienen por ricos 'many hold (them) rich'; = tener por)
assí: assí — thus, so (= así) · also assí — so greatly, so much (Pidal 'de tal modo, mucho'; assí envergonçó 'was so abashed')
aquel: aquel — that one, whoever · also aquel — that (demonstrative adjective; aquel día de cras 'tomorrow'; aquella mayor az 'that biggest line')
santos: santo — saint (masc. pl.); los sos santos 'his saints' · also adjective, holy (los santos padres 'the holy fathers')
rogó: rogar — he begged (preterite 3rd sg.; tanto las rogó 'so much he begged them'; = rogó)
adeliñó: adeliñar — he made straight for, headed to (preterite)
poral: pora + el — toward the (pora 'toward, for' + article; Pidal restores the a: por[a]l castiello 'toward the castle'; = para el, hacia el)
palaçio: palaçio — hall, palace; the main room of a house (= palacio)
do: do — where, as (relative adverb, Latin de ubi; = donde) · also do — wherever, whenever (generalizing, with subjunctive: do yo vos enbiás 'wherever I might send you'; the exact sense is uncertain) · also dar — I give (present 1st sg.; d'aquí vos do mi graçia 'from here I give you my favor'; = doy) · also do — for don, 'lord' (title before a name; el obispo do Jero[me] 'the bishop don Jerome')
cum: cum — as, like (spelling of como, Latin quomodo; con tal cum esto 'with such as this'; = como)
medio: medio — middle; en medio de 'in the middle of' · also medio — 'the half' (noun; el medio echó en campo 'he threw the half onto the field'; = la mitad)
vídolos: ver + los — he saw them (vido 3rd sg. preterite + object los, the accent written on the verb's stressed vowel; = los vio)
reçibió: reçebir — he received, accepted (preterite 3rd sg.; = recibió)
delant: delant — ahead, in front (apocopated adverb; = delante) · also delant — before, in front of (preposition; Parávas delant al Campeador 'he took his stand before the Campeador'; = delante de)
inojos: inojo — knee (= hinojo; fincar los inojos 'to kneel')
fincó: fincar — he planted, set firm (preterite; fincar los inojos 'to kneel') · also fincar — he stayed, remained (el Campeador fincó con su mesnada 'the Cid stayed with his troop'; = quedó)
piedes: pie — feet (old plural, Latin pedes; los piedes e las manos 'the feet and the hands'; = pies) · also de piedes de cavallo 'at full gallop' (Pidal 'a uña de caballo')
merçed: merçed — mercy, favor; Merçed! 'have mercy, I beg you' (= merced) · also merçed — grace, favour (con la merçed del Criador 'by the grace of the Creator') · also en vuestra merçed 'at your disposal, at your command' (en vuestra merçed somos nos; Pidal 'estamos a vuestro mandar')
largos: largo — abundant, ample, generous (masc. pl.; averes largos 'plentiful goods'; = largos)
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
fo: seer (and ir, which shares this preterite) — he/it was; went (preterite 3rd sg.; = fue, restored by Pidal as f[o]; of this part's three occurrences, fo entrado and fo acusado are periphrastic/passive ser + past part. constructions, while fo algo is a plain copula with a pronoun predicate, 'was something') · also commo fo tu voluntad, ca fo tu voluntad 'as/for it was your will' (ser + noun subject, 'it was'; Pidal restores f[o]) · also se fo acomendar 'went to commend himself' (ir); fo de noch 'it was night' (ser de + noun, 'night had come'); fo desenparada (passive, 'was abandoned') · also fo — went (ir; mañanas fo Minaya 'in the morning Minaya went'); fo de moros 'it came from the Moors' (ser de + noun of origin; Pidal restores f[o]) · also fo — it was, ser + adjective predicate (Buena fo la de Valençia 'good was the (capture) of Valencia'; Pidal restores f[o]) · also fo — was (the man) of, belonged to (ser de of a vassal; el que de Albar Fáñez fo 'he who was Álvar Fáñez's man'; = fue)
ya: ya — O! (vocative particle, Arabic yā); also 'now, already' · also ya — 'would', reduced imperfect of aver as conditional ending, 3rd sg., after infinitive + clitic (pagar se ya 'would be satisfied'; = -ía)
sabedes: saber — you know (present 2nd pl., old -edes ending; = sabéis)
abiltados: abiltar — shamed, dishonored (past part. masc. pl., from abiltar 'to dishonor', cf. vil; seremos abiltados 'we shall be dishonored'; = envilecidos)
majaron: majar — they beat (preterite 3rd pl.; tanto las majaron 'so much they beat them'; = majaron)
del: de + el — of the (contraction) · also del standing for de + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (del albergada = de la albergada) · also del — 'from, for, because of' (cause; del gozo 'from the joy'; del çerviçio 'for the service')
majadas: majar — beaten, battered (past part. fem. pl., agreeing with nos; fuéremos majadas 'we are beaten'; = majadas; modern majar 'to pound')
desnudas: desnudo — bare, drawn (fem. pl., of swords; = desnudas)
dexaron: dexar — they left (preterite 3rd pl.; por muertas las dexaron 'they left them for dead'; = dejaron)
robredo: robredo — oak wood, oak grove (masc.; el robredo de Corpes 'the oak wood of Corpes'; = robledo, robledal)
corpes: Corpes — the oak wood where the daughters are abandoned (robredo de Corpes); Pidal: it has disappeared today, and lay south-west of San Esteban de Gormaz
bestias: bestia — beast, mount (fem. pl.; riding/pack animals; = bestias) · also bestia — wild beast (bestias fieras 'wild beasts', las bestias de la fiera guisa 'the savage beasts')
fieras: fiero — great, mighty, extraordinary (fem. pl.; fieras ganançias 'great gains'; modern fiero 'fierce', so a weaker sense here (uncertain nuance); = grandes) · also fiero — wild, savage (bestias fieras 'wild beasts'; = fieras)
aves: ave — bird; birds as omens, augury (fem. pl.; buenas aves 'good omens', from the old practice of reading birds' flight; = aves, closest agüeros)
mont: Mont — mount, hill (Latin montem; = monte); Mont Mayor, the place Martín Muñoz held: Montemayor, a Portuguese town he governed for Alfonso VI, according to Pidal · also Mont Real — Monreal, name of the place above which the Cid's hill stands (Pidal: Monreal del Campo, on the Jiloca); see real · also Mont Alván — Montalbán, town in Teruel (a Mont Alván; = Montalbán) · also mont — wood, wild wooded country (apocopated monte, common noun; en aqueste mont 'in this wood'; = monte)
gelos: ge + los — them to him (ge, ancestor of modern se, + los; = se los) · also ge = 'to them' (que gelos diessen 'that they should give them to them', the knights) · also ge 'from him', dative of separation (gelos reçibe 'he receives them from him')
levedes: levar — you take, carry (2nd pl., -edes; here a command, tres mill moros levedes 'take three thousand Moors'; probably present subjunctive used as imperative; = llevad)
tienes: tener + se — he holds himself (present 3rd sg. tiene + reflexive se, the e of se run into tiene; tener por 'to consider as'; = se tiene) · also tener — you hold, have (present 2nd sg.; espada tienes en mano 'you hold a sword in hand'; = tienes)
mayor: mayor — larger, greater (aquella mayor az 'that greatest line'; = mayor) · also Mayor — part of the place name Mont Mayor, Montemayor (the Portuguese town, Pidal) · also la mayor — 'the great', standing epithet of Valencia (Valençia la mayor)
sabidor: sabidor — one who knows, informed, in charge (= sabedor; vos seed sabidor 'you be the judge, the one who decides') · also sabidor de — acquainted with, familiar with (d' aquellos moros yo so sabidor 'I know those Moors well')
una: uno/una — one, a (fem.) · also a una — together, as one (adverbial; hivan a una compaña 'they went together'; a una grant ondrança 'together with great honor'; = juntos) · also en una conpaña — 'together, in company' (en una conpaña tornados son amos 'both have come back together'; cf. a una)
comidió: comedir — he reflected, pondered (preterite 3rd sg.; penssó e comidió 'he thought and pondered', Pidal 'pensó y meditó'; = meditó)
verdad: verdad — truth (dezir vos he la verdad 'I shall tell you the truth'; = verdad) · also non será verdad — 'it shall not be so' (Pidal: 'esto no será así'; esto non será verdad) · also por verdad — truly, indeed (í albergaron por verdad una noch 'they truly lodged there one night')
digo: dezir — I say (present 1st sg.; yo non vos digo nada 'I say nothing to you'; = digo)
pesa: pesar — it grieves, it distresses (present 3rd sg., impersonal; mucho pesa a los de Teca 'it greatly grieves the men of Ateca'; = pesa)
tú: tú — thou, you (2nd sg. subject pronoun; used in prayer to God)
quier: querer — (he) wishes (present 3rd sg. without -e, subjunctive in value; qui quier 'whoever, anyone at all', = quienquiera; = quiera)
fosse: seer — he were (imperfect subjunctive of seer; MS fuesse, Pidal's older form) · also ir — he should go (imperfect subjunctive 3rd sg., the preterite stem of seer shared with ir; que f[o]sse con Minaya 'that he should go with Minaya'; = fuese) · also seer — I were (imperfect subjunctive 1st sg.; commo si fosse delant 'as if I were present')
entre: entre — between, among; entre X e Y 'X and Y together' · also entre — entrar, may it enter (present subjunctive 3rd sg.; ante que entre la noch 'before night comes on'; = entre)
salve: salvar — may he save (present subjunctive 3rd sg., optative; sí el Criador vos salve 'so may the Creator save you'; = salve)
fer: fazer — to do, make (short infinitive form; = hacer; fer lo he = lo haré, split future)
sazón: sazón — due season, prime condition; de sazón 'in good condition, fit' (palafré de sazón 'a palfrey in prime condition', probably; = sazón)
reyno: reyno — kingdom (= reino) · also reyno — reign (Pidal: mio reyno adelant 'en lo sucesivo de mi reinado', 'in the rest of my reign'; = reinado)
mie: mie — my (fem. sg. of mio, before a noun; = mi)
vayan: ir — let them go (present subjunctive 3rd pl., jussive; vayan los mandados 'let the messages go'; = vayan)
cuemdes: cuemde — count (noble title; masc. pl., old form of conde spelled with m; in cue[mdes] the mdes is Pidal's; = condes)
ifançones: ifançón — minor nobleman, hidalgo (masc. pl.; cuemdes e ifançones 'counts and lesser nobles'; = infanzones)
mandaré: mandar — I shall order (future 1st sg.; yo les mandaré dar conducho 'I will order provisions given them'; = mandaré)
i: e/i — and (variant of e before some sounds) · also i — there, therein (adverb, Latin ibi, like French y; meted i las fedes, 'put your pledged faith into it')
den: den — from there, from it (de + en, the short form of ende 'thence', as dent = de + ent; non pueden den quitar 'they cannot get clear of it'; = de allí, de ello)
vedar: vedar — to forbid, prevent, cut off (infinitive; agua … vedar 'to deny water'; Latin vetare; closest prohibir, impedir)
